missing_enum: typescript: missing enum name in schema %q
catalog_embed: typescript: catalog column %q in table %q cannot embed a table
header: // Code generated by sqlc. DO NOT EDIT.
filename_nul: typescript: query filename contains a NUL byte
filename_url: typescript: query filename %q contains a URL-significant character (#, ?, or %%)
index_json: export type { JsonValue, JsonObject, JsonArray } from "./json.ts";
pg_insert_id: PostgreSQL has no connection insert ID; use INSERT ... RETURNING with :one
unused_param: parameter %d has no placeholder in the SQL
client_mysql:
import type { Connection } from %s;

export type Database = Pick<Connection, "execute">;
client_better:
%simport type { Database } from %s;
export type { Database };
client_bonakodo:
import type { Database } from %s;
export type { Database };
lemma_invalid: invalid @lemma annotation; use a single line with requires, ensures, or contract and a nonempty payload
lemma_boundary: //@ contract External database boundary. SQL, driver behavior, codecs, and user contracts are trusted here, not verified.
lemma_state: //@ contract Each call may observe different database state. Contracts describe normal return only; they do not prove effects, isolation, revocation, or authorization.
lemma_query: //@ contract Query %s from %s; command %s; engine %s; driver %s.
lemma_argument: //@ contract Parameter %s: args[%s] has TypeScript type %s; resolved nullable=%s; optional property=%s.
lemma_field: //@ contract Result field %s has TypeScript type %s; resolved nullable=%s; conversion kind=%s.
lemma_codec: //@ contract %s uses a custom codec. Its conversion and validation contract needs a separate model.
lemma_array: //@ contract %s has %s SQL array dimensions; nullable elements follow the generated TypeScript type.
lemma_slice: //@ contract args[%s] is a SQL slice: elements bind in array order; an empty slice emits NULL and binds no values.
lemma_binding: //@ contract SQL placeholder occurrence %s uses parameter %s (args[%s])%s.
lemma_pg_bindings: //@ contract PostgreSQL binds each numbered parameter once in first-occurrence order; repeated placeholders reuse that slot.
lemma_other_bindings: //@ contract Each scalar placeholder occurrence binds one encoded value; repeated parameters repeat their values.
lemma_one: //@ contract Returns the first decoded row, or %s when no row exists. This does not assert SQL uniqueness.
lemma_many: //@ contract Returns all decoded rows, preserving driver order. No rows yields an empty array; SQL determines ordering and duplicates.
lemma_exec: //@ contract Executes the statement and returns no value. This makes no claim about which records change.
lemma_execrows: //@ contract Returns the driver affected-row count as bigint. Count semantics follow the driver and database.
lemma_lastid: //@ contract Returns the driver connection insert ID; its type and range follow driver settings. It is not an authorization token.
lemma_execresult: //@ contract Returns rowsAffected as bigint and lastInsertId as bigint or null. Driver and database define count and ID semantics.
lemma_errors: //@ contract Argument encoding finishes before SQL execution. Driver or codec failure throws or rejects; these clauses do not guarantee success.
lemma_numbers: //@ contract JavaScript numbers retain runtime precision and range limits. Formal numeric models and custom types need explicit review.
lemma_factory: // LemmaScript: contracts belong to the named query functions; this factory only binds the connection.
lemma_embed: //@ contract Embedded result %s has TypeScript type %s; child fields describe decoding and outer-join null handling.
lemma_async: //@ contract Async result: the TypeScript return is a Promise. LemmaScript 0.6.1 does not unwrap external Promise results or model await; resolved-row postconditions need a separate model.
